display.title: Episode 322: The Vanishing Bottle of Wine (Chol HaMoed Pesach)
display.summary_short: A Chol HaMoed Pesach show: seeing ourselves as leaving Mitzrayim today, a B'chol Dor Vador song, a visiting family in Studio 604, and how a shamash's dream foiled a blood libel.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the middle of Pesach 5748. Uncle Yossi explains why we celebrate with a Seder, matzah and leaning: had Hashem not taken our fathers out of Mitzrayim, we would still be slaves, so the freedom is ours today. One of the Twelve Pesukim, B'chol Dor Vador, teaches that each of us must see himself as if he left Mitzrayim. A short dramatized skit and song follows, in which two children dream they rescue a deer caught in a bush and remember being freed from Egypt. The Hakochainik march is the Yom Tov song 'Mi'Mitzrayim Ge'altanu'. A visiting family joins Uncle Yossi in Studio 604 to say the Shema and several of the Twelve Pesukim. Story time tells of Reb Arele, a devoted shul shamash who dreams three times that a voice asks him, 'Where is the wine for Pesach?' He discovers that a wicked man has replaced the wine in the Aron HaKodesh with blood, swaps it back, and on Pesach the plot to accuse the Jews before the king falls apart. The show closes with a reminder about eruv tavshilin before Shvi'i shel Pesach, the Pesach newsletter mitzvah charts, and Dial-a-Jewish-Story.
display.lesson: Hashem, the Guardian of Israel, never slumbers or sleeps; in every generation He saves us from those who rise against us.

advisories.note: A blood libel: an enemy of the Jews plants a bottle of blood in the shul to accuse them before the king; the plot fails.
